brief: A high-tension, professional visual featuring the expansive roof of a large, modern industrial factory in North India, bathed in the warm, urgent light of a late afternoon sun. The composition emphasizes scale and industry, with a subtle, sleek graphic overlay of a countdown clock or calendar highlighting the critical November 10th decision date. The copy hook is 'Don't Let the December 31st Price Hike Hit Your Factory.' The message avoids technical jargon like 'DCR' and instead frames the upcoming regulatory shift as a significant cost increase (over 10,000 rupees per kilowatt) that can be avoided by acting now. Solaride is positioned as the trusted, engineering-backed partner (IIT/PEC) that helps factory owners secure compliant, cost-effective energy before the deadline. The mood is serious, urgent, and authoritative, leveraging the trust of local expertise and the Diwali offer of 10% off to drive immediate action. The call to action is to book a free site survey by November 10th to lock in current rates and avoid the upcoming cost surge.
sourceFacts: I want to make a ad for specifically big factory as on 31st December, the government is banning the panels which are non-DCR panels, and because of which the cost of the solar panels or cost of the solar installation will go more than 10,000 rupees per kilowatt.So I don't want to confuse customers by non-DCR and DCR, I just want to marketize this and want to attract the customers who are factory owners. If the customer wants solar before 31 December, he has to take decision before 10th november
